recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-34098 unless a future CDS decision changes PlanDefinition trigger semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-34098 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request for FHIR-core PlanDefinition. It requested clarification that when multiple trigger elements are present on a PlanDefinition action, any trigger should invoke the action.
initial_application: The Jira comment links HL7/fhir PR #1802. Git history shows merge commit e793bfc7ab512424f052bc68d699a77a5e2be01a included commit 6b2c72268228cec5c9af4b844ad17244b469e0a2, which changed source/plandefinition/structuredefinition-PlanDefinition.xml to add the multiple-trigger ANY semantics sentence.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists plandefinition=PlanDefinition, so the PlanDefinition StructureDefinition source is in build scope. Later source cleanups reformatted or regenerated the PlanDefinition XML but preserved the requested wording. Zulip discussion before the Jira confirms the intended semantics were OR, and a later Zulip clarification says the post-R4 CI build wording reflects that intent. Confluence has no direct FHIR-34098 references. FHIR-39029 was found by keyword search but concerns SubscriptionTopic repetitions, not PlanDefinition.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current PlanDefinition.action.trigger definition says, "When multiple triggers are specified on an action, any triggering event invokes the action," which implements the Jira resolution without redundant narrative.

related_jiras.note: Keyword search found this separate SubscriptionTopic multiple-repetition question, but it is a different artifact and work group and does not affect PlanDefinition.action.trigger.
